title: Ten Crack Commandments
year_note: The year is the original's. This recording is an AI-made soul cover posted on YouTube, and its upload title is all we know about it. An album track on Life After Death (March 25, 1997), never a single.

titles: Biggie Smalls – Ten Crack Commandments (50s Soul Version)

notes.made: DJ Premier produced it, in the years when he worked out of Studio A at D&D in New York on an Akai MPC60 and S950 sampler. Premier says Biggie counted off the numbers himself and asked him to pair each one with a scratched snippet of Chuck D's voice from Public Enemy's 1991 'Shut 'Em Down'. Rolling Stone also credits a Les McCann composition, 'Vallarta', in the track. Biggie reportedly drew the idea from a sidebar of dealers' rules in a July 1994 Source article by Khary Kimani Turner, who is a credited writer.
notes.context: Crack had shaped the neighborhoods rap came from for over a decade, and this is the coldest treatment of it on Biggie's records: no chorus, no 16-bar verses, ten numbered rules for staying alive in the trade. Chuck D sued the estate and Premier because he did not want his voice on a song that seemed to back drug dealing, and settled in November 1998. Premier said he would never have sued a dead man, and that he and Chuck made peace at Jam Master Jay's wake in 2002.

listen_for.note: The count is the structure of the song, with a scratched Chuck D fragment marking each rule; any cover has to keep that list shape in place of a chorus.
There is no sung hook in the original at all, so a soul version has to invent its own melody where Premier's loop and Biggie's spoken rules sat.

leads_to.title: Shut 'Em Down
leads_to.why: The Def Jam single from Apocalypse 91... The Enemy Strikes Black that supplied Chuck D's voice, and the root of the lawsuit.

notes.unverified: The release and year of Les McCann's 'Vallarta' (couldn't find it), and whether Premier made this beat at D&D specifically.

culture.title: Ten Duel Commandments
culture.line: Lin-Manuel Miranda built the dueling-rules number in Hamilton as a homage to it.

culture.title: Chuck D's lawsuit
culture.line: Chuck D sued over his sampled voice and settled in November 1998; Premier later said he had wanted the blame on himself rather than on Biggie's estate.

culture.title: A deep cut that lasted
culture.line: Billboard put it ninth among his 25 best songs in 2020, and it went Silver in the UK on streams and sales since 2004.
